title: kernel-v1 comparative benchmark run constants (v1)
description: Versioned source of truth for every numeric constant the comparative benchmark harness (bench/benchmark.sh, bench/analyze.sh) reads. The harness refuses to start if this schema is missing or malformed. No numeric constant in the harness may be hardcoded; every threshold, sample size, and confidence level is anchored here. The release gate (task 60) asserts sub-5% p99 latency increase and sub-5% throughput decrease for observe and enforce modes relative to the no-agent baseline; those thresholds live here as default_p99_latency_max_pct and default_throughput_decrease_max_pct.

sample_size.description: Number of measured iterations per (workload, comparator) pair. Warmup iterations are excluded. The harness runs exactly this many measurement iterations after warmup; each iteration produces one JSONL row. A minimum of 3 is required so the paired-difference confidence interval is computable.

warmup_iterations.description: Number of warmup iterations run (and discarded) before measurement begins. Warmup primes CPU caches, JIT paths, and filesystem page cache so the measured iterations reflect steady-state behavior. Set to 0 to disable warmup.

confidence_level.description: Confidence level for the paired-difference confidence interval computed by bench/analyze.sh. The analysis reports the upper bound of the CI for p99 latency increase and the upper bound of the CI for throughput decrease at this confidence level. 0.95 corresponds to a 95% CI.

default_p99_latency_max_pct.description: Release-gate threshold: maximum permitted p99 latency increase (as a percentage of the no-agent baseline p99) for observe and enforce modes. The analysis marks a workload/comparator pair as failing when the 95% CI upper bound of the p99 increase exceeds this value. Anchored here so the harness never hardcodes the 5% gate.

default_throughput_decrease_max_pct.description: Release-gate threshold: maximum permitted throughput decrease (as a percentage of the no-agent baseline throughput) for observe and enforce modes. The analysis marks a workload/comparator pair as failing when the 95% CI upper bound of the throughput decrease exceeds this value. Anchored here so the harness never hardcodes the 5% gate.

ops_per_iteration.description: Number of individual operations each workload performs per measured iteration. Per-operation latencies are collected within an iteration to compute p50/p95/p99/p99.9. A larger value yields tighter percentile estimates at the cost of longer iteration duration.

workloads.description: The workload identifiers the harness iterates over. Each maps to bench/workloads/<name>.sh. The harness validates that every listed workload script exists and is executable before starting.

comparators.description: The comparator identifiers the harness iterates over. Each maps to bench/comparators/<name>.sh. no-agent is the mandatory baseline; the analysis computes paired differences against it. The harness validates that every listed comparator script exists and is executable before starting.
